q: By the time the project reaches completion, 30% + 50% of the RPF has already been paid. Following the practice of closing off the remaining balance at completion, how much is the Architect still owed?
n: 30% + 50% = 80% has already been paid (PHP 640,000.00 of the PHP 800,000.00 RPF). The remaining balance paid at project completion is the other 20%: PHP 800,000.00 − PHP 640,000.00 = PHP 160,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.2)
scenario: For an Architectural Interior engagement, the Architect and Client have agreed on a Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of PHP 800,000.00.

q: How much should the Architect be paid for coordinating and relating the Specialist Consultant’s work to the design concept?
n: When the Owner/Client hires SCs separately, the Architect’s coordination fee is 5% of the SC’s fee: 5% × PHP 400,000.00 = PHP 20,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.2.3)
scenario: The Owner/Client separately hires a Specialist Consultant (SC) whose professional fee for the project is PHP 400,000.00. The Architect coordinates and relates the SC's work to the Architect's design concept.

q: Physical Planning services under Sec. 7.3.2 do NOT include which of the following?
o: The tiered per-hectare Recommended Professional Fee computation
Engineering services and other allied services such as landscape design, transportation planning, and environmental investigations
The Conceptual Master Development Plan output
n: Sec. 7.3.2.4 clarifies that the Physical Planning fee pertains only to physical planning outputs and does not include engineering services and other allied services (e.g., landscape design, transportation planning, environmental investigations). (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.4)

q: Per the Physical Planning fee schedule, one hectare is equivalent to how many square meters?
n: The schedule notes that 1 hectare = 10,000 sq. meters, used to convert the per-sq.-meter rates into per-hectare fees. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.1)

q: The 10%–15% RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1 applies to which set of services?
o: Architectural Interior (AI), Acoustic Design, Architectural Lighting Layout and Design, and Site Development Planning (SDP)
Regular Design Services under SPP Doc. 202
Full-Time Supervision and Construction Management only
n: Sec. 7.3 sets the Recommended Professional Fee specifically for Architectural Interior, Acoustic Design, Architectural Lighting Layout and Design, and Site Development Planning. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3)

q: Under Sec. 7.3.3, what is the basic compensation method for “Other Specialized Architectural Services” (all classified as additional/extra services)?
o: A fixed lump-sum regardless of scope
A flat percentage of the Project Construction Cost (PCC)
Man-months (22 man-days × 8 man-hours × a factor for overhead/indirect costs), or the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense Method
n: Sec. 7.3.3 states basic compensation shall be through man-months (22 man-days × 8 man-hours, multiplied by a factor covering overhead and other direct/indirect costs), or using the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense Method. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.3)

q: What is the Physical Planning RPF for this project?
n: 25 hectares falls in the “over 10 up to 50 hectares” bracket: PHP 450,000.00 + (PHP 30,000.00 × 15 hectares in excess of 10) = PHP 900,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.1)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, on moderately flat terrain.

q: Using the minimum end of the RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1, how much is the Architect’s fee?
n: The minimum RPF is 10% of the Cost of Work: 10% × PHP 6,000,000.00 = PHP 600,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Acoustic Design services for a project with a Cost of Work of PHP 6,000,000.00.

q: How many distinct Methods of Compensation for Specialized Architectural Services are listed under Sec. 7.2.1?
n: Sec. 7.2.1 lists 8 methods: Percentage of Cost of Work, Unit Cost Method Based on Cost of Work, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee plus Expenses, Lump Sum or Fixed Fee, Retainer, Per Diem/Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses, and Mixed. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.2.1.1–7.2.1.8)

q: Using the minimum 20% terrain adjustment, what is the adjusted RPF for this rugged-terrain project?
n: A 20% increase on the base RPF of PHP 900,000.00 gives PHP 900,000.00 × 1.20 = PHP 1,080,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.2)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, but the site is rugged with steep terrain. (Base Physical Planning RPF before terrain adjustment: PHP 900,000.00.)

q: Using the maximum end of the RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1 for the same project, how much is the Architect’s fee?
n: The maximum RPF is 15% of the Cost of Work: 15% × PHP 9,400,000.00 = PHP 1,410,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Site Development Planning (SDP) services for a project with a Cost of Work of PHP 9,400,000.00.

q: The Consulting Architect (CA) may hold a valid Specialist Certificate issued by whom, and upon what condition?
o: The PRC Board of Civil Engineering, upon inter-professional endorsement
The Board and/or the Commission, upon due accreditation of the IAPoA
The local government unit, upon payment of a specialist fee
The IAPoA, upon accreditation by the Board
n: The Specialist Certificate may be issued by the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture and/or the Professional Regulation Commission, upon due qualification or accreditation by the IAPoA (Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects). (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7 (definition))

q: How much is due upon the Framework Development Plan (FrDP)?
n: FrDP is paid at 30% of RPF: 30% × PHP 900,000.00 = PHP 270,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.3)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, with a computed Physical Planning RPF of PHP 900,000.00.

q: How much is due to the Architect upon submission of the final design?
n: Payment upon final design submission is 50% of the RPF: 50% × PHP 800,000.00 = PHP 400,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.2)
scenario: For an Architectural Interior engagement, the Architect and Client have agreed on a Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of PHP 800,000.00.

q: When using the Percentage of Cost of Work method, the Architect’s fee excludes the fee of whom?
o: Any Engineering and/or Specialist Consultants (SCs) working with the Architect
The Architect’s own draftsmen and junior staff
n: Sec. 7.2.2 states that when using the Percentage of Cost of Work method, the Architect’s Fee excludes the fee of any Engineering and/or Specialist Consultants (SCs) working with the Architect. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.2.2)

q: How much is due upon the Detailed Master Development Plan (DMDP)?
n: DMDP is paid at 20% of RPF: 20% × PHP 900,000.00 = PHP 180,000.00. (FrDP + CMDP + PMDP + DMDP = 270,000 + 270,000 + 180,000 + 180,000 = PHP 900,000.00, the full RPF.) (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.3)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, with a computed Physical Planning RPF of PHP 900,000.00.

q: The Physical Planning fee schedule under Sec. 7.3.2 applies to building sites for which of the following?
o: Only projects located within Metro Manila
Only single-family residential lots below 1,000 sq.m.
Only government infrastructure projects funded by national appropriations

Industrial estates, commercial, religious, institutional, government/civic centers, sports complexes, tourist centers/estates/resorts, amusement parks, educational facilities, residential and housing subdivisions, and the like
n: Sec. 7.3.2 covers Physical Planning for building sites such as industrial, commercial, religious, institutional and government/civic centers, sports complexes, tourist centers/estates/resorts, amusement parks, educational facilities, residential and housing subdivisions, and the like. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) range for Architectural Interior, Acoustic Design, Architectural Lighting Layout and Design, and Site Development Planning?
o: 10% to 15% of the Cost of Work
A flat 12% of the Cost of Work
15% to 20% of the Cost of Work
5% to 10% of the Cost of Work
n: Sec. 7.3.1.1 sets the RPF at 10% to 15% of the Cost of Work, depending on the complexity of the work required by the project. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)

q: A Physical Planning engagement is abandoned by the Client before completion of a particular stage. How is the Architect compensated?
o: The Architect may bill and be paid progress payments proportional to the percentage of progress of completion of the work, with a pro-rated fee component paid for the abandoned/incomplete stage
The Client is entitled to a full refund of any payments already made
The Architect receives no compensation, having not finished the stage
The Architect must complete the stage for free before any billing
n: Sec. 7.3.2.6 allows the Architect to bill and be paid progress payments proportional to the percentage of progress of completion; if the work is abandoned or not completed at a particular stage, the pro-rated PF component is still paid to the Architect by the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.6)

q: Using the Physical Planning RPF schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee for this project?
n: 8 hectares falls in the “over 5 up to 10 hectares” bracket: PHP 250,000.00 + (PHP 40,000.00 × 3 hectares in excess of 5) = PHP 370,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.1)
scenario: A proposed industrial estate has a site area of 8 hectares.

q: Using the maximum end of the RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1 for the same project, how much is the Architect’s fee?
n: The maximum RPF is 15% of the Cost of Work: 15% × PHP 2,000,000.00 = PHP 300,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Architectural Interior (AI) design services for a project with a Cost of Work of PHP 2,000,000.00.

q: What is the overall subject matter governed by SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7?
o: Construction Management Services for large-scale projects
Specialized Architectural Services — additional/extra architectural services requiring specific expertise beyond regular design services
n: SPP Doc. 203’s Sec. 7 governs Specialized Architectural Services — additional or extra services requiring specific expertise for further enhancement of a project’s architectural interior/exterior components, distinct from Regular Design Services (SPP Doc. 202). (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7 (title & definition))

q: The Physical Planning rates in Sec. 7.3.2.1 assume what site condition, and what adjustment applies otherwise?
o: A moderately flat site; a 20% to 30% fee increase applies if the land is rugged or has steep terrain
A sloping site; a 10% discount applies for flat sites
An urban site; a 50% surcharge applies for rural sites
A reclaimed site; no adjustment is made regardless of terrain
n: Sec. 7.3.2.2 states the rates are based on the assumption that the land is moderately flat; if the land is rugged with steep terrain, the fee shall increase by 20% to 30%. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.2)

q: Using the minimum end of the RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1, how much is the Architect’s fee?
n: The minimum RPF is 10% of the Cost of Work: 10% × PHP 9,400,000.00 = PHP 940,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Site Development Planning (SDP) services for a project with a Cost of Work of PHP 9,400,000.00.

q: For purposes of Specialized Architectural Services under SPP Doc. 203, the term “Architect” specifically refers to whom?
n: In the context of Specialized Architectural Services, the term “Architect” refers to the Consulting Architect (CA). (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7 (definition))

q: What is the Physical Planning Schedule of Payment under Sec. 7.3.2.3, in order of the four planning stages?
n: The schedule is 30% upon Framework Development Plan (FrDP), 30% upon Conceptual Master Development Plan (CMDP), 20% upon Preliminary Master Development Plan (PMDP), and 20% upon Detailed Master Development Plan (DMDP) — totaling 100%. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.3)

q: How much is due to the Architect upon submission of the preliminary design?
n: Payment upon preliminary design submission is 30% of the RPF: 30% × PHP 800,000.00 = PHP 240,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.2)
scenario: For an Architectural Interior engagement, the Architect and Client have agreed on a Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of PHP 800,000.00.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the Methods of Compensation for Specialized Architectural Services listed under Sec. 7.2.1?
o: Unit Cost Method Based on Cost of Work
Value-Pricing based on a percentage of gross rentals
n: Value-pricing based on gross rentals is a compensation method used for Post-Construction Services, not one of the 8 methods listed for Specialized Architectural Services (Percentage of Cost of Work, Unit Cost Method, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, Professional Fee plus Expenses, Lump Sum/Fixed Fee, Retainer, Per Diem/Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses, and Mixed). (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.2.1.1–7.2.1.8)

q: How much is due upon the Preliminary Master Development Plan (PMDP)?
n: PMDP is paid at 20% of RPF: 20% × PHP 900,000.00 = PHP 180,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.3)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, with a computed Physical Planning RPF of PHP 900,000.00.

q: An AI project under Sec. 7.3 is abandoned by the Client partway through, before the Architect’s services are completed. How should the Architect be paid?
o: The Architect is entitled to the full 100% RPF regardless of the stage of abandonment
The Architect is paid the amount proportional to the percentage of progress/work completed at the stage the project was abandoned
The Architect forfeits all fees not yet formally invoiced
The Architect must return all fees already received
n: Per Sec. 7.3.1.3, if the work is not completed, the Architect shall be paid the amount proportional to the work completed at the stage when the project was abandoned. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.3)

q: Under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method, compensation may also be computed through man-months. How is one man-month defined for this purpose?
o: 22 man-days multiplied by 8 man-hours, multiplied by a factor for other direct and indirect costs
n: Compensation via the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense method (and the “Other Specialized Architectural Services” method) may be computed through man-months, i.e., 22 man-days × 8 man-hours, multiplied by a factor to cover other direct and indirect costs such as overhead. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.2.4 / Sec. 7.3.3)

q: Under Sec. 7.3.2.5, the detailed design of the building/s and landscaping elements is not part of Physical Planning Services. Where is it instead treated?
o: Only under Construction Management Services (SPP Doc. 204-B)
Only under Full-Time Supervision Services (SPP Doc. 204-A)
Separately, under Regular Design Services (SPP Doc. 202) or Specialized Architectural Services — Site Development Planning (SPP Doc. 203)
n: Sec. 7.3.2.5 states the detailed design of the building(s) and landscaping elements is treated separately, either under Regular Design Services (SPP Doc. 202) or under Specialized Architectural Services (Site Development Planning) (SPP Doc. 203). (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.5)

q: Using the Physical Planning RPF schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee for this project?
n: A site area of 3 hectares falls within the “first 5 hectares or less” bracket — a basic rate of PHP 5.00 per sq.m. net to the architect, i.e., a flat PHP 250,000.00 for that bracket. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.1)
scenario: A proposed housing subdivision has a site area of 3 hectares.

q: Using the minimum end of the RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1, how much is the Architect’s fee?
n: The minimum RPF is 10% of the Cost of Work: 10% × PHP 2,000,000.00 = PHP 200,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Architectural Interior (AI) design services for a project with a Cost of Work of PHP 2,000,000.00.

q: Aside from man-months and MDPE, which of the following is one of the “other applicable” modes mutually agreed upon by the Architect and Client for Other Specialized Architectural Services under Sec. 7.3.3?
o: Rate Cost times a multiplier plus reimbursable expenses
n: Sec. 7.3.3 lists per diem plus reimbursable expenses, retainer plus reimbursable expenses, and rate cost times a multiplier plus reimbursable expenses as the other applicable modes mutually agreed upon. Percentage of PCC is instead the Construction Management Services fee basis (SPP Doc. 204-B), not a Sec. 7.3.3 mode. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.3(a)-(c))

q: What is the Physical Planning RPF for this project?
n: 70 hectares falls in the “over 50 hectares” bracket: PHP 1,650,000.00 + (PHP 15,000.00 × 20 hectares in excess of 50) = PHP 1,950,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.1)
scenario: A proposed government center project has a site area of 70 hectares.

q: Using the maximum end of the RPF scale under Sec. 7.3.1.1 for the same project, how much is the Architect’s fee?
n: The maximum RPF is 15% of the Cost of Work: 15% × PHP 6,000,000.00 = PHP 900,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.1)
scenario: An Architect is engaged to provide Acoustic Design services for a project with a Cost of Work of PHP 6,000,000.00.

q: Under SPP Doc. 203, Specialized Architectural Services deal with which of the following?
o: Specific expertise for the further enhancement of the architectural interior and exterior components of a project
The preparation of subdivision plans and land titling documents
The structural design of buildings and other engineered structures
General project management and cost control functions
n: SPP Doc. 203 defines Specialized Architectural Services as dealing with specific expertise for the further enhancement of the architectural interior and exterior components of a project. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7 (definition))

q: Using the maximum 30% terrain adjustment, what is the adjusted RPF for this rugged-terrain project?
n: A 30% increase on the base RPF of PHP 900,000.00 gives PHP 900,000.00 × 1.30 = PHP 1,170,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.2)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, but the site is rugged with steep terrain. (Base Physical Planning RPF before terrain adjustment: PHP 900,000.00.)

q: Sec. 7.3.1.2 states the Manner of Payment for AI/Acoustic/Lighting/SDP services as 30% upon submission of the preliminary design, 50% upon submission of the final design, and 50% upon completion of the project. What is notable about these stated percentages, and how is it resolved in practice?
o: They total only 80%, so the Architect must waive the remaining 20%
They total 130%, and in practice the completion payment is treated as simply closing off whatever balance remains to reach 100%
They total exactly 100%; no adjustment is needed
The percentages apply only to Physical Planning services, not to AI/Acoustic/Lighting/SDP
n: As stated, the three percentages (30% + 50% + 50%) add up to 130%, not 100%. In practice, the project-completion payment is treated as simply closing off whatever balance remains unpaid, rather than a literal additional 50% of the RPF. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.1.2)

q: Under Sec. 7.1, in what two ways may the Architect enter into a contract with the Owner for Specialized Architectural Services?
o: Only as a subcontractor to the general contractor, or as a project owner’s representative
Only through a design-build arrangement, or as an in-house company architect
Working in a dual capacity as Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect, or working solely as Consulting Architect for the specialized service
As a government-accredited assessor, or as an independent auditor of the project
n: Sec. 7.1 allows the Architect to work either in a dual capacity — as Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect (CA) for the specialized services — or solely as Consulting Architect for the Specialized Architectural Services. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.1)

q: How much is due upon the Conceptual Master Development Plan (CMDP)?
n: CMDP is also paid at 30% of RPF: 30% × PHP 900,000.00 = PHP 270,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3.2.3)
scenario: A proposed tourist estate/resort project has a site area of 25 hectares, with a computed Physical Planning RPF of PHP 900,000.00.
